headline: Approved fee schedules for liens and burial grounds, a $90,401.40 transfer for FATV, and utility poles on Fairmount St. and Alpine Rd.
summary: Three ordinances changing Chapter 169 will go to first and second readings. A grade steps ordinance for fiscal 2027 was held on a 9-1 roll call vote. A request to repeal the tobacco sales chapter was referred to Legislative Affairs.
decisions: Referred appointment letters for five special police officers and one burial grounds trustee to the Appointments Committee.
Filed the audited financial statements of the Fitchburg Retirement System for 2024.
Placed on file notices of two park grants, about $150,000 and $25,000.
Approved the Appointments Committee report on three board appointments, 10-0.
Adopted the minutes of the July 21, 2026 meeting, 10-0.
Withdrew a request for a rule change requiring in-person voting on official matters.
Withdrew a request to end work-from-home arrangements.
Approved the Legislative Affairs Committee report, 10-0.
Sent Ordinances 144-26 A through C to first and second reading and ordered them advertised, 10-0.
Granted Unitil's petition for a new utility pole at 40 Fairmount St., 10-0.
Granted Unitil's petition for four new utility poles at 515 Alpine Rd., 10-0.
Appropriated $90,401.40 from the PEG access reserve to pay FATV's second quarter 2026 franchise fee, 10-0.
Accepted a state law section letting the treasurer record unclaimed funds as city revenue, 8-2.
Adopted a fee schedule for certificates of liens, from $25 to $150 by property type, 10-0.
Accepted a personal property exemption for items valued under $2,000, 10-0.
Adopted a fee schedule for the Public Burial Grounds, 10-0.
Referred a request from the public health director to repeal the tobacco sales chapter to Legislative Affairs.
Referred a petition for temporary repairs of a private way on Greenhurst Ave. to Public Works.
Held the amended grade steps ordinance for fiscal 2027 by a 9-1 roll call vote.

City of Fitchburg  
                             Massachusetts 01420  
 
                     CITY COUNCIL  
            
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Fitchburg was held at the Legislative Building 
at 700 Main Street and over the Zoom meeting platform and live streamed at FATV Studios, 
Fitchburg, on September 2, 2026.   
 
The meeting was called to orde r by President Zarrella at 7:04 P.M.  The meeting opened with a 
salute to the Flag led by Council  President Zarrella. The City Clerk called the roll 10 Councilors 
were present, (Councilor Walsh absent). Board consists of 11 members.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
I. PUBLIC FORUM 
  
No one spoke during public forum. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
II. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
The next meeting of the Widowed Helping Widowed Support Group will take place tomorrow 
(Thursday, September 3) from 4 until 5:30 p.m. in Room 205 at the Fitchburg State University 
Recreation Center, 130 North Street. Kelley Lynn, Kathy Boisvert, and Bernie Schultz will co-
facilitate the meeting. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
Fitchburg City Councilor Bernie Schultz is hosting a City Council Community Meeting on 
Thursday, September 17, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. right here in the Legislative Building, 700 
Main Street.  Health Director Steve Curry and Irene Congdon, Municipal Assistance 
Coordinator from the Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection, will make a 
presentation on trash and recycling issues, and then answer questions following their 
presentation. 
---- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Councilors at Large 
    Sally H. Cragin

The Fitchburg Historical Society is revving up its programming this fall.  
We are starting with our Annual Meeting, which is fully open to the public and will be taking place 
on Thursday, September 24, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. These meetings are historic events themselves! 
They have been going on for over 100 years, and today's residents are invited to take part in the 
tradition. It’s a great chance to meet the board members and Historical Society members, 
volunteers and staff. The annual meeting will take place at the Historic Phoenix Building, at 781 
Main Street. For more information, visit the website at Fitchburghistoricalsociety.com.  
 
The public is also invited to the Historical Society for a talk by author Chris Boucher, who will 
speak on Harry Bucky Lew, Basketball's first Black pro and Fitchburg's role in the integration of 
Pro Sports. The talk will take place on Thursday, October 1 at 6 p.m. and is free to the public. 
Bucky Lew's mother was from Fitchburg and his grandparents came to Fitchburg from the South 
during the Civil War.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
The public is invited to an upcoming Community Meeting on Wednesday, September 17th, 
focused on “Fitchburg Goes Green.” Joining us for the discussion will be Board of Health Director 
Steve Curry and Municipal Assistance Coordinator Irene Congdon. Residents are encouraged to 
attend, learn more about Fitchburg’s waste reduction and sustainability efforts, and bring their 
questions for our guests. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
If you have a worn American flag the Fitchburg Community Lions Club, has a new program called 
Stars for our Troops. They repurpose retired, tattered American flags by cutting out their 
embroider stars. Each star is sealed in a protective pouch with a keepsake card – a reminder to 
those in uniform that their service is valued and not forgotten. To donate a flag, you can contact 
Councilor Amy Green 978-230-1815 or email backntouch@verizon.net. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Sunday, September 13, 2026 starting at 2 PM you can join he friends of Fitchburg cemetery for a 
special historic walking tour entitled the poetry of the bereaved at Dean Hill cemetery. You can 
learn about the history of revolutionary soldiers and their families and hear the verses inscribed on 
the slate headstones read aloud. It’s an excellent program for youth families and seniors. 
Admission is free, but donations are accepted. After the program there will be an opportunity to 
create original drawings, paintings, and photographs of the historic site and some art supplies will 
be provided.  
For more information you can email friendsoffitchburgcemeteries@gmail.com 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Also on September 20, 2026, starting at 2 PM the acclaimed local ensemble, the Thurston consort 
returns to perform at Forest Hill Abbey also known as the Mausoleum. The Abbey’s marble 
interior and intimate setting makes for unique musical experience for all. Admission is free and 
donations accepted. These programs are supported by the Fitchburg Cultural Council.  
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Fitchburg invites you to attend a highly informative, free Small Business Workshop: “Focus on 
Marketing” event occurring on Mon. Sept. 21st (6:00-7:30PM) at Fitchburg City Hall (718 Main 
St. 3rd floor).  
  
The session will provide local business owners as well as aspiring entrepreneurs with useful 
guidance on the latest approaches to effectively capture your targeted customers to grow your 
business.  Features speakers include a series of marketing experts who will share insights on the 
range of tools and approaches being utilized by today’s successful businesses.  Don’t miss this 
opportunity to learn timely information while also being able to connect with your peers within the 
local business community.  
  
Space will be limited for this popular topic. Please contact Mary Jo Bohart – Economic 
Development Director at 978-829-1896 or email: mbohart@fitchburgma.gov.

145-26. Unitil to petition for a new proposed pole 40 Fairmount St. - #1A on Fairmount St.,

 40 Fairmount St. - Proposed Pole 
 
President Zarrella declared the Public Hearing open at 7:24 PM 
 
Mr. John Kimball, from Unitil, spoke and explained that the new pole is necessary because the 
existing wires are antiquated and heavy. Unitil will be installing new wires and requires the new  
pole to support them safely. 
 
No one spoke in favor to the petition. 
 
No one spoke in opposition to the petition.

X. ORDER – OTHERS 
 
Motion and second to  pull Orders 141-26, 142-26 and 143-26 from Committee by unanimous  
consent 10/0. 10 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
 
141-26. ORDER THAT: The Fitchburg City Council accepts the provisions of Section 9A 
of Chapter 200A of the General Laws to (1) allow the Fitchburg Treasurer, subject 
to the notice requirements of M.G.L. c.200A, §9A, to record as revenue in the 
General Fund of the City any funds held in the custody of the City which have 
remained unclaimed for at least one year after the date payment was issued or the 
funds were delivered, and (2) to allow the Treasurer to hear and decide all claims on 
abandoned funds that may arise prior to the date the abandoned funds escheat to the 
City. 
 (Ref. petition 126-26) 
 
Motion and second to adopt order by 8 in favor and 2 opposed (Councilor Fleming & Green).  
10 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
 
Order signed by the Mayor September 23, 2026. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
142-26. ORDER THAT:  the City Council of the City of Fitchburg hereby accepts M.G.L. 
c. 60, §23B, Certificate of liens; fee schedule;  
 
 The Collector of taxes shall furnish certificates of liens as provided in section 
twenty-three (23) according to the following fee schedule: 
 
 for land upon which is situated no more than a single-family residence and 
outbuildings, a fee of twenty-five dollars; 
 
 for land upon which is situated no more than a two-family residence and 
outbuildings, a fee of twenty-five dollars; 
 
for land upon which is situated no more than a three-family residence and 
outbuildings, a fee of twenty-five dollars; 
 
for land upon which is situated a residence for four or more families, a fee of one 
hundred dollars; 
 
for land upon which is situated a commercial, industrial or public utility structure, a 
fee of one hundred and fifty dollars; 
 
for farms, forest land and all other real property, a fee of fifty dollars. 
 
THAT in no case shall the fee exceed one-half of one percent of the assessed value 
of the real estate and the money so received shall be paid into the City Treasury. 
(Ref. petition 127-26) 
 
Motion and second to adopt order by unanimous consent 10/0. 10 members present. Board consists 
of 11 members. 
 
Order signed by the Mayor September 23, 2026. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
